summary:
The MATE Improvement Act (S. 946, 119th Congress) amends Section 303 of the Controlled Substances Act (21 U.S.C. 823) to clarify and expand the roster of organizations and professional programs recognized for purposes of the training requirement applicable to prescribers of controlled substances—the training obligation added by the Medication Access and Training Expansion (MATE) Act enacted as part of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023.

As a threshold technical correction, Section 2(a)(1) redesignates the second of two subsections erroneously both designated as subsection (l) as subsection (m), resolving a duplicate-designation drafting defect.

Section 2(a)(2) then amends the redesignated subsection (m)(1) in two respects:

For subparagraph (A) (governing the training-provider recognition and curriculum provisions for physicians and dentists), the bill: (i) in clause (iv)(I), adds the American Academy of Family Physicians, the American Podiatric Medical Association, the Academy of General Dentistry, the American Optometric Association, and the Council on Podiatric Medical Education to the list of organizations whose training satisfies the requirement, with conforming punctuation changes; (ii) in clause (iv)(III), adds the American Academy of Family Physicians; and (iii) in clause (v), adds "podiatric medicine" to the enumerated professional schools and adds a "podiatric medicine curriculum" to the recognized curricula, extending curriculum-based satisfaction of the requirement to podiatric medical education.

For subparagraph (B) (governing recognition for pharmacists and certain nursing prescribers), the bill: (i) in clause (i), adds the American Pharmacists Association, the Accreditation Council on Pharmacy Education, the American Psychiatric Nurses Association, the American Academy of Nursing, and the American Academy of Family Physicians to the recognized organizations; and (ii) in clause (ii), adds an accredited school of pharmacy to the accredited institutions whose curriculum satisfies the requirement.

Section 2(b) sets a retroactive effective date, providing that the amendments "shall take effect as if enacted on December 29, 2022"—the enactment date of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023, which contained the underlying MATE Act training provisions—so that the expanded recognition operates from the inception of the training requirement.

The bill contains no authorization of appropriations, no appropriation, and no sunset provision. Its operation is confined to conforming and expanding statutory text; it does not alter the substantive scope or duration of the eight-hour training requirement itself, only the set of qualifying providers, organizations, and educational curricula.
